definitions.meaning: A graph of displacement s against time t for a motion; its gradient at any moment is the velocity.
The rate of change of displacement with time, read from an s-t graph as its gradient: change in displacement divided by change in time.
Rise over run between two points on a graph: on an s-t graph the gradient is the velocity, and on a v-t graph the gradient is the acceleration.
The rate of change of velocity with time, read from a v-t graph as its gradient; a straight s-t graph has zero acceleration because its velocity is constant.
A graph of velocity v against time t for a motion; the area under it is the displacement and its gradient is the acceleration.

mechanismSteps: Two graphs, one motion - a straight s-t line and a flat v-t line describe the same uniform journey.
Gradient of the s–t graph is the velocity - build the gradient triangle between two points: rise in displacement over run in time.
Area under the v–t graph is the displacement - each thin rectangle is velocity times a small time step, and the stacked area is the displacement.
The SUVAT pair — and the gradient trap - v = u + at and s = ut + (1/2)at^2 for constant acceleration, and a straight s-t graph means constant velocity, not acceleration.
objectives: Read the velocity of a motion as the gradient of its displacement-time graph
Find the displacement of a motion as the area under its velocity-time graph
Apply the SUVAT pair v = u + at and s = ut + (1/2)at^2 to motion with constant acceleration
subject: math
title: A-Math kinematics: reading motion from s–t and v–t graphs

trap.explanation: The slip: Straight-line growth reads as speeding up. The fix: The gradient of s-t is velocity: a straight s-t graph has constant velocity and zero acceleration. So a straight s-t graph shows uniform motion with zero acceleration.
trap.misconception: A straight s-t graph means constant acceleration.

workedExample: Work step by step (s2): the gradient of the s-t graph is the velocity. Step 1: read two points on the line: (0, 10) and (6, 40), displacement in metres and time in seconds. Step 2: form the gradient: (40 - 10)/(6 - 0) = 5. Step 3: attach the unit: the velocity is 5 m/s. Because the s-t graph is a straight line, this gradient is the same between any two points, so the velocity is 5 m/s throughout the motion.
